availabilityPolicy: Only exact positive IDs, plus the three separately reviewed one-hop species-to-generic raw salmon edges, satisfy these scopes. Generic salmon No overrides derived species coverage. Raw and fully cooked sausages, bone-in and boneless cuts, and different cuts create no reverse/sibling or raw-to-cooked ownership. An exact No on an explicitly listed independent sausage alternative removes that food only.
integrationRequirement: Append the exact approval to the existing market coverage ledger without editing prior batches. Extend raw/cooked protein admission and per-ingredient title policies; keep species/bone/cut evidence separate from USDA analytical yield. Apply six scoped and two auxiliary candidate removals plus all exact text patches. Preserve prior produce permissions and bind the implemented blueprints to the proposed hash. All seven reviewed mixed market groups must remain protected even when a group has zero allowed scopes, so stale/custom grouped candidates fail closed. Auxiliary ground-beef removals must not introduce global protection or change unrelated exact ground-beef ownership/pricing.

instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.before: Cube pork shoulder (or loin) into 1.5-inch chunks, season with salt & pepper, and toss into the slow cooker with cubed potatoes (or cauliflower florets for low-carb).
instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.after: Thaw frozen raw pork in the refrigerator before starting. Cube pork shoulder into 1.5-inch chunks, season with salt & pepper, and toss into the slow cooker with cubed potatoes (or cauliflower florets for low-carb).

instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.before: Cut chuck roast into 2-inch cubes, pat dry, and sear in batches in a hot Dutch oven until deeply browned.
instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.after: Thaw frozen raw beef in the refrigerator before starting. Cut boneless beef chuck roast into 2-inch cubes, pat dry, and sear in batches in a hot Dutch oven until deeply browned.

instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.before: Brown ground beef (or turkey/sausage) with diced onions and bell/poblano peppers in a large pot or Dutch oven; drain excess fat.
instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.after: Thaw frozen raw meat in the refrigerator before starting. Remove casings from raw sausage links and crumble the sausage or ground meat. Brown ground beef, ground turkey, raw ground pork or crumbled raw pork sausage/chorizo with diced onions and bell/poblano peppers; drain excess fat. Use a food thermometer: cook ground beef/pork and pork sausage to at least 160°F, or ground turkey to at least 165°F.

instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.before: Bavarian Smoked Kielbasa, Braised Cabbage, Apple & Potato Skillet
instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.after: Bavarian Sausage, Braised Cabbage, Apple & Potato Skillet

instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.before: Slice smoked sausage into coins and sear in a deep Dutch oven or heavy skillet until browned; transfer to a plate.
instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.after: Use only sausage labeled fully cooked or ready-to-eat: smoked sausage, kielbasa or andouille. If frozen, thaw in the refrigerator before slicing. Slice into coins and sear in a deep Dutch oven or heavy skillet until browned; follow the product label for heating, then transfer to a plate.

instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.before: Brown Italian sausage in the Instant Pot (or Dutch oven) with diced onion, carrots, and garlic.
instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.after: Thaw frozen raw protein in the refrigerator before starting. Remove casings from raw Italian pork sausage links and crumble the sausage, or cut boneless chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces. Brown the selected sausage, chicken or ground turkey with diced onion, carrots and garlic. Use a food thermometer: cook pork sausage to at least 160°F, or chicken/ground turkey to at least 165°F.

instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.before: Place cubed butternut squash (or sweet potatoes, or cauliflower florets for the low-carb replacement), diced onions, diced tomatoes, and chicken thighs into the slow cooker.
instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.after: Thaw frozen raw chicken in the refrigerator before starting. Place cubed butternut squash (or sweet potatoes, or cauliflower florets for the low-carb replacement), diced onions, diced tomatoes, and boneless skinless chicken thighs or breast into the slow cooker.

instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.before: Whisk broth/coconut milk with curry powder, garam masala, garlic, and ginger; pour over chicken and cook on LOW for 4.5 hours.
instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.after: Whisk broth/coconut milk with curry powder, garam masala, garlic, and ginger; pour over chicken and cook on LOW for about 4.5 hours, until the chicken reaches at least 165°F on a food thermometer.
Raw Pork Sausage, Fully Cooked Sausage or Ground Turkey

instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.before: Brown sausage with finely diced potatoes/sweet potatoes (or mushrooms or diced fresh summer squash, including zucchini or yellow summer squash, for the low-carb vegetable base) and diced peppers/onions in a skillet for 10 minutes until tender. If using spinach or kale for the low-carb base, saute the chopped greens until tender and excess moisture evaporates; spread into a greased 9x13 baking dish.
instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.after: Thaw frozen protein in the refrigerator before starting. For raw pork sausage links, remove casings and crumble; for fully cooked sausage, slice or dice. Brown the selected meat with finely diced potatoes/sweet potatoes (or mushrooms or diced fresh summer squash, including zucchini or yellow summer squash, for the low-carb vegetable base) and diced peppers/onions until tender. Cook raw pork/sausage to at least 160°F or raw ground turkey to at least 165°F on a food thermometer; heat fully cooked sausage according to its label. If using spinach or kale for the low-carb base, saute the chopped greens until tender and excess moisture evaporates; spread into a greased 9x13 baking dish.

instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.before: Pour egg mixture over the sausage-vegetable hash, top with remaining cheddar, and bake at 375°F for 35–40 minutes until set in the center.
instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.after: Pour egg mixture over the sausage-vegetable hash, top with remaining cheddar, and bake at 375°F for about 35–40 minutes until the casserole reaches at least 165°F in the center on a food thermometer.

instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.before: Season beef chuck roast generously with salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and rosemary; place in the slow cooker surrounded by whole baby bella mushrooms, diced onion, and celery.
instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.after: Thaw frozen raw beef in the refrigerator before starting. Season boneless beef chuck roast generously with salt, black pepper, garlic powder, and rosemary; place in the slow cooker surrounded by whole baby bella mushrooms, diced onion, and celery.

instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.before: Preheat oven to 400°F. Toss halved Brussels sprouts (or broccoli) and diced potatoes or fresh summer squash (including zucchini or yellow summer squash) on a large sheet pan with olive oil, salt, and garlic powder; roast 12 minutes.
instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.after: Thaw frozen raw salmon fillets in the refrigerator before starting. Preheat oven to 400°F. Toss halved Brussels sprouts (or broccoli) and diced potatoes or fresh summer squash (including zucchini or yellow summer squash) on a large sheet pan with olive oil, salt, and garlic powder; roast 12 minutes.

instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.before: If serving the low-carb spinach or kale side, saute those greens separately until tender. Roast 11–13 minutes more until salmon flakes easily at 135°F internal temp so it stays moist when reheated.
instructionTitleAndLabelPatches.after: If serving the low-carb spinach or kale side, saute those greens separately until tender. Roast until the salmon reaches at least 145°F on a food thermometer; check after about 11–13 minutes and continue cooking as needed.
